requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the 'What are you importing?' page keeps the live-animals title, caption, heading, ITAHC inset, label, buttons, Cancel link and back link (to the origin page), and its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a trader importing germinal products what they can search for, and changes nothing else on the page. The 9 October afternoon ruling lets the germinal set's copy of today's commodity page, with this hint, go ahead on today's commodity data; no trace shows a germinal error state on this page, so its errors are the live-animal page's.
requirements.deltaNote: The real animals frontend has no germinal products set today.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, and the live-animals set's catalogue holds only live-animal commodities, so neither set offers the other's commodities.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written; each set's catalogue holds only its own commodities. Splitting today's lines between the sets is set architecture, not list content, so it goes ahead without waiting on MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live-animals commodity catalogue holds 12 germinal lines (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) and there is no germinal set; the germinal lines move out of live animals into the germinal set's own catalogue.

requirements.statement: Once commodities come from MDM, the germinal products catalogue holds the 12 specified germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species listed under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish or bee germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: A germinal products notification needs germinal commodities to choose from. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields V4 page sets which germinal commodities the germinal data applies to, naming the same twelve entries in all five of its applicability lists; the GBN-AG schema has separate EMBRYO and OVA type codes, so embryos and ova are separate items; Design Release 2.1 gives the species and the names. Its Cat and Dog embryos and ova are mock data the 9 October ruling does not copy, and V4 gives them no fields (c-230). V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat' is shown as separate Cat, Semen and Dog, Semen items. V4 writes the codes without their leading zero and never says how they map to the codes a notification carries, which c-germinal-products-002 settles in favour of the eight-digit codes the real catalogue and MDM use; its single 05119985 does not tell the eleven non-cattle entries apart, so a line is identified by product type and species as well as by code. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes this 18-item catalogue wait on MDM (c-282).
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2), and the germinal commodity catalogue and search are re-distilled from that list; until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Total gross weight' in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', before Number of packages, for every germinal commodity in the catalogue. It is optional: left blank, no error is shown, and the trader enters the figure.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 measures germinal products by weight and asks it on every germinal species block; V4 makes the total gross weight in kilograms an optional numeric field the trader supplies, with the example 24.50, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. V4's weight row is the one germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes the field is asked for (confluence-6497338582-p5-012); as the germinal set holds only germinal commodities and the other five germinal fields apply to all twelve entries, it is asked on every germinal species block, as Design Release 2.1 does.

requirements.statement: The germinal set stores each species line's 'Total gross weight' answer as that line's gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal, and shows it back in the service; it is not published on GBN-AG, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no gross weight.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks, errors and reviews the answer as 'Total gross weight', and what the real record stores is persistence, so the prototype's internal netWeight key does not decide the quantity. The ruling publishes only what v0.2.0 already carries.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each commodity complement and species line records only whole-number animal and package counts, with no gross weight (repo-backend-p1-039, p1-040, p1-043, p1-044, cited in the backend's own area). The line's quantity stays its number of packages (c-234); only the gross weight is a decimal.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block asks 'Number of packages', with no hint and no '(when required)', after Total gross weight, and the trader enters the count; germinal species are not asked the number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package, not by head. V4 holds the germinal quantity on each commodity line and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only; its quantity row is the other germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes it is asked for, and as the set holds only germinal commodities it is asked on every species block.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's Commodity details page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, its legend styled at label size (not a heading), with the hint 'How will the products be stored' and the options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order, after all commodity blocks. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown. The answer is stored on every commodity line of the notification.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks once how germinal products will be stored; V4 captures the temperature on each commodity line as an optional single-select the trader answers, with exactly those three values, the example Frozen, and the same twelve germinal commodities the other germinal fields apply to, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only.

requirements.statement: A germinal-product commodity has one Selected commodities row listing all its chosen species (for example '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Bos taurus'), its block is headed '<name> (<code>)' such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and its species sections are separated by section breaks.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays germinal products out commodity by commodity.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is started by the germinal set's own start (reached from the type question's Germinal products option or from 'Create new' on the germinal set's own notification list at /germinal-products), which creates the draft and skips the notification type question. It opens at the origin page, which shows only 'Save and continue' and whose back link returns to the germinal set's own notification list, and then runs through 'What are you importing?' to 'Main import reason' as live animals does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal products their own entry point; the real services start each set from its own route rather than the prototype's create-notification?category= link. The prototype's germinal dashboard is the germinal set's own list, and the INS germinal list's 'Create new' leaves this programme with the INS home (c-281).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the main import reason offers only Internal market and Transit, in that order. The question 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?' and the hints (Internal market: 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transit: moving through Great Britain to a third country) keep their live-animal wording, and the page ends with Save and continue, Save and return to overview and 'Cancel and return to overview'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the reasons for germinal products and changes no other wording on the page; the prototype decides wording, and nothing overrides its choice to keep 'the animals' in the question.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, Internal market reveals 'Purpose in the internal market' with only Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production, in that order, each with its hint; a submitted purpose outside these four counts as not chosen and shows 'Select a purpose in the internal market'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the internal market purposes for germinal products.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set has no Additional details page and no Additional details task: the hub's section 2 holds 'Commodity details', and 'Identification details' where it applies, only, and 'Save and continue' on a valid identification page reached through the journey goes straight to Arrival details; opened from its overview task, the review or the template review, the identification page returns there instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the certification question for germinal products and no germinal commodity has unweaned options, so the page has nothing to ask; the ruling's option B plan leaves the page out of the set.

requirements.statement: A germinal product needs one set of identification details per species, whatever its quantity: its panel shows one editable form headed 'Enter details for <species>' (no count, such as 'Enter details for Bos taurus'), prefilled with what was saved, with no panel button and no saved-entries table. The page's own 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' both save the values typed into each germinal species' form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 identifies germinal products once per species, not per package; the real store already holds one line per species. V4 holds the four germinal identifiers at unit level without saying how many unit records a germinal line carries, so the ruling and Design Release 2.1 set the count at one per species.

requirements.statement: Every germinal products commodity asks for 'Donor name/ID' (text), 'Collection date', 'Production date' and 'Identification number/mark' (text), in that order: four unit-level identifiers the trader enters, which apply to every germinal commodity in the catalogue.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields V4 page sets the identifiers a germinal products notification captures, holds all four at unit level, has the trader supply every one of them, marks them as affecting the germinal journey only, and gives each the same twelve germinal commodity entries, so one applicability list covers all of them; Design Release 2.1 asks them in this order.

requirements.statement: If design keeps it, each germinal date field gains a 'Choose date' calendar toggle (the MOJ date picker) opening a month grid with previous and next year and month buttons, 'Select' and 'Close', enhancing the single text input the field already has; if design answers that a plain date field or the GOV.UK date input will do, that is built instead, or the calendar is dropped.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 renders these dates with the MOJ date picker, but MoJ advises against its date picker for dates a user reads from a document, so the 9 October afternoon ruling makes the calendar wait on design question 12 in its own increment in the waiting-on-design theme, as every JavaScript-only prototype behaviour does. The input it enhances is the one built now (req-252, req-2097).
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 12 (germinal dates): whether the MoJ date picker's calendar stays, or a plain date field or the GOV.UK date input will do instead.

requirements.statement: A Donor name/ID over 58 characters shows 'Donor name/ID must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the donor name or ID to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length for it, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: Germinal dates accept one- or two-digit day and month (such as 1/9/2026), any real date past or future, and a production date is not checked against the collection date; they read back as entered.
requirements.why: Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 sets a range or ordering rule on these dates; V4 only asks for a valid DD/MM/YYYY date, and its own example 12/12/2026 for both dates is in the future, so a future date is allowed.

requirements.statement: Each germinal identification field is optional on its own, so a partly or wholly blank entry saves without a missing-value error and never blocks 'Save and continue' (only the length and date rules apply to what is entered). But every selected germinal species, a lone species included, counts as identified only once its entry holds at least one of the four identifiers, and that one bar decides both submit and the hub's 'Identification details' Complete status. The identification page shows no message for this rule.
requirements.why: V4 marks all four germinal identifiers Optional and marks no germinal field mandatory to submit, while its own opening rule requires at least one germinal identifier per animal without naming which fields count or how 'per animal' maps to its unit records; the 9 October ruling settles that silence by making one identifier enough for both Complete and submit.

requirements.statement: A germinal product's identification panel keeps the species heading and the 'Change number of animals' link (to Commodity details), worded as for live animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not reword the panel for packages, and the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: Germinal products is its own set in trade-imports-animals-frontend, SET_ID 'germinal-products', mounted at /germinal-products beside live-animals, with its own journey, obligations, flow, cookies, gateway (routes-germinal-products.js) and set services. Its journey pages sit at /germinal-products/notifications/{journeyId}/{slug} using the live-animals slugs, each a copy of its live-animals feature folder plus the germinal differences; its overview, check answers, declaration and confirmation pages are its own copies too. Every live-animal field not marked as applying to the animal journey only is carried over; the CPH number and permanent address, which apply to the animal journey only, are not, so the set has no CPH number page and no permanent address page. The plants frontend has no germinal set, so no germinal-only difference changes plants.
requirements.why: Duplicating pages via features is the app's architecture and is desired, and option B of the germinal options paper was chosen over option A; the prototype's flat paths are not copied. V4's germinal section marks its seven fields as affecting the germinal journey only and names only the CPH number and permanent address as not required for germinal products, without saying which other live-animal fields the germinal journey drops or keeps and without a header row of its own, so the germinal field list is read from the ruling's copy rule plus V4's own per-field markings rather than from the germinal table alone (req-1832, req-1833). The copy of each live-animals page is taken after this programme has built the live twin. The 9 October afternoon ruling leaves plants unchanged by rows it has no equivalent of and never mirrors animals-only data into it.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification is created with Draft status and the same kind of reference as a live-animals one, GBN-AG followed by the two-digit year and six characters, shown in the status strip from the first page; no GBN-GP reference is ever issued.
requirements.why: Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references; GBN-GP references are demonstration data only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today only live-animals notifications exist; each is minted a GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX reference at creation (repo-frontend-p2-009, trace-e2e-p13-004, repo-tests-p2-115).

requirements.statement: Once commodities come from MDM, searching 'semen' in the germinal set lists the eight semen commodities in name order (Cat, Semen; Cattle, Semen (05111000); Dog, Semen; Goat, Semen; Horse, Semen; Pig, Semen; Rabbit/Rodent, Semen; Sheep, Semen, all others 05119985), offering 12 species rows, and the live region announces '12 results available'; Cattle, Semen offers 'Bovidae' and Rabbit/Rodent, Semen offers 'Rabbit/Rodent' as group rows.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal search shows each commodity with its code and species. The list is V4's catalogue, which waits on MDM; the results announced as the trader types are the germinal copy of the search-as-you-type increment, which also waits on design question 3.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2), and the germinal commodity catalogue and search are re-distilled from that list; until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927). The as-you-type results and their live-region announcement also wait on design's answer to design question 3 (commodity search as you type).

requirements.statement: Once commodities come from MDM, ticking a germinal species, such as Domestic cattle (Bos taurus) under Cattle, Semen, shows '1 selected' with a 'Cattle, Semen (05111000):' line and a 'Bos taurus' chip, as the live-animal search does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal selections the same way as live-animal ones; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it wait with the V4 germinal catalogue.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2), and the germinal commodity catalogue and search are re-distilled from that list; until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927).

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight that is not a number greater than 0 (digits with an optional decimal part; no sign, commas or units), such as 0, shows 'Enter a number greater than 0', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 and Design Release 2.1 both require the weight to be above 0; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight over 1,000 shows 'Total gross weight must be 1,000kg or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the total gross weight at 1,000 kg. Its conditions cell is empty, so neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message or says what happens at exactly 1,000; the message and the inclusive limit follow the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: A Total gross weight accepts up to 2 decimal places (1.5 and 24.50 are accepted); more shows 'Total gross weight must have 2 decimal places or fewer', linked to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 gives the weight to 2 decimal places, with 24.50 as its example, and the ruling holds it as a decimal; Design Release 2.1 accepts 1.5. V4 states no rounding rule, so a figure with more decimal places is refused with a message rather than rounded, following the GOV.UK pattern.

requirements.statement: Number of packages is required: left blank, it shows 'Enter the number of packages', linked from the error summary to that species' field and shown inline.
requirements.why: V4 makes the line's quantity mandatory to proceed, the only mandatory field in its germinal section, and Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more, such as 'x', shows 'Enter a whole number greater than 0', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts packages in whole numbers from 1; V4 gives the quantity a maximum but no minimum, no decimal-place rule and an empty conditions cell, so it sets no minimum of its own and the prototype decides.

requirements.statement: A Number of packages over 1,000 shows 'Number of packages must be 1,000 or less', linked to that species' field and shown inline; 1,000 itself is accepted.
requirements.why: V4 caps the germinal quantity at 1,000, with 10 as its example. Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 gives the message, so it follows the GOV.UK pattern for a maximum.

requirements.statement: Valid germinal commodity details continue to Identification details.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's germinal journey runs Commodity details, then Identification details.

requirements.statement: An invalid germinal identification submission re-renders the page with the error summary; its errors are listed in field order (Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification number/mark), each linking to its own field, which is shown in error with the message inline.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows germinal identification errors in the standard GOV.UK way.

requirements.statement: A submitted main reason outside the germinal set's two (such as Re-entry) is saved as no reason.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 accepts only the reasons offered to the notification.

requirements.statement: Once the germinal catalogue separates embryos from ova (when commodities come from MDM), each germinal products trade line in the published GBN-AG payload carries the typeCode for its product type: SEMEN for semen, EMBRYO for embryos and OVA for ova. Embryos and ova are then separate commodities, each its own trade line, never one 'Embryos/Ova' line.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema names these codes, and the 9 October ruling makes the schema, not the prototype's mock data, decide them; the 9 October afternoon ruling applies the separate EMBRYO and OVA items only once the catalogue is re-distilled from MDM. Live-animal lines carry LIVE_ANIMAL (req-1894).
requirements.deltaNote: Today trade lines carry no typeCode (repo-backend-p6-109, c-273). Until this lands, today's lines carry the interim codes of req-1928.
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities come from MDM (ruling 9 October afternoon, point 2), and the germinal commodity catalogue and search are re-distilled from that list; until then the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927).

requirements.statement: Publishing to PIMS the germinal products details it has no field for (temperature, donor name/ID, collection and production dates, identification mark, decimal kilogram quantity, each line's gross weight) through a new GBN-AG profile version.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the PIMS schema update is EUDPA-686, a Jira ticket outside the backlog that starts after this programme lands, and its shape is not yet known.

requirements.statement: Capturing an approved establishment on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the data fields page's change log records the germinal Approved Establishment field as de-scoped on 7 September 2026, with no reason given and no field row left on the page, which outranks any source that still describes it.

requirements.statement: Capturing a package type on a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the data fields page's change log records the germinal Package type field as de-scoped on 7 September 2026, and Design Release 2.1's germinal commodities carry no packaging fields. An unresolved inline comment hangs on the change-log row and its text is not in the fetched page, so whatever it questions is not recorded.

requirements.statement: A k6 performance journey for the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the performance suite has no germinal set base, steps or endpoints anywhere under src/, and its catalogue names no germinal route, so nothing the germinal set adds breaks one of its k6 scripts; the suite changes only where a row breaks a script it already has (c-225).

requirements.statement: The germinal set's end-to-end, accessibility and security specs live in the tests repo's existing animals Playwright project, under tests/animals/e2e/germinal-products, tests/animals/a11y/germinal-products and tests/animals/security/germinal-products; no new Playwright project is made, and INS-side germinal work is proven in the ins project. The accessibility specs walk the germinal journey and hold each page to WCAG 2.2 AA on initial load and with answers filled, under the suite's existing axe rules, and the security specs drive the germinal routes through the ZAP scan.
requirements.why: The germinal set is still the animals frontend, and the ruling places its specs there.
requirements.deltaNote: The accessibility and security suites today cover only the live-animals journey (repo-tests-p6-021, p6-042, p6-091, cited in the tests repo's own area).

requirements.statement: Until commodities come from MDM, the germinal set's 'What are you importing?' page, with its germinal search hint, offers the 12 germinal lines the live-animals catalogue holds, with their existing names and codes and with embryos and ova as one combined 'Embryos/Ova' line, found through a server-side search behind the Search button, with no results shown as the trader types.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling splits the germinal commodity work so the germinal set is not blocked by the MDM catalogue: the page's wording (req-069) and place in the journey go ahead on today's commodity data, and today's search already works without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal set today; the 12 germinal lines sit in the live-animals catalogue (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) and move to the germinal set (req-092).

requirements.statement: Until the germinal catalogue separates embryos from ova, each germinal products trade line in the published GBN-AG payload carries an interim typeCode: SEMEN for a semen line, and EMBRYO for a combined 'Embryos/Ova' line, so a combined line submitted in this time records ova as embryos.
requirements.why: The GBN-AG schema has no combined embryos-and-ova code, and today's catalogue still holds combined lines until commodities come from MDM; the 9 October afternoon ruling sets EMBRYO as the default, which Sam has not objected to.
requirements.deltaNote: Today trade lines carry no typeCode (repo-backend-p6-109, c-273).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set's identification page, Collection date and Production date are each a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026', which works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives both dates this hint, and the 9 October afternoon ruling builds them now as single text inputs. Same change as req-252 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, an Identification number/mark over 58 characters shows 'Identification number/mark must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the identification number or mark to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message in the Donor name/ID pattern. Same change as req-255 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date not in the form day/month/four-digit year shows 'Enter a collection date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY collection date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's production date message. Same change as req-256 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date not in the form day/month/four-digit year, such as 2026-09-01, shows 'Enter a production date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid DD/MM/YYYY production date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-257 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date in the right format that is not a real date, such as 99/99/2026, shows 'Collection date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid collection date and Design Release 2.1 gives the message. Same change as req-258 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date in the right format that is not a real date shows 'Production date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: V4 requires a valid production date; the message follows Design Release 2.1's collection date message. Same change as req-259 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page's 'Selected commodities' quantity column is headed 'Number of packages' and shows each species' saved count, where live animals show Number of animals.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products by package on the identification page too. Same change as req-1776 (another area's); the cross-area pass merges them.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, 'Save and return to overview' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue' on every page that shows both buttons, the set's own Commodity details and Identification details pages included: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error in the summary and inline for each one and what they entered kept, and with nothing missing or invalid the answers are saved and the overview is shown.
requirements.why: The two save buttons behaving alike, with no page an exception, is what the owner decided; a trader who saves and returns otherwise leaves a page holding answers the service has not checked, and the germinal-only weight, package, length and date rules would be made by one button and not the other. The 26 October ruling names only the live animals and high-risk plants frontends, so whether the rule reaches the germinal products set rests on c-germinal-products-001.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal 'Total gross weight' is a gross or a net weight: DR2.1 labels it gross weight but stores it as netWeight.

positions.says: The field is labelled 'Total gross weight' but stored and validated as netWeight.
The weight is submitted as netWeight[<species>], so gross and net weight are conflated.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype default.
A germinal products notification captures a 'Total gross weight (kg)' field.
In the germinal set, weight is a total gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal.

conflicts.outcome: Gross weight: the germinal page keeps the label 'Total gross weight' and its DR2.1 copy, and the answer is stored as each line's gross weight in kilograms, as a decimal (ruling 9 October, V4). The prototype's netWeight key is an internal storage name, and data-model shape is never the prototype's to decide. The gross weight is stored and shown but not published, because gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0 has no gross weight. The trace claim still backs the label and kg suffix, so only the netWeight storage claim is set aside.

conflicts.about: How a germinal notification is routed: the prototype's flat pages and create-notification?category=germinal-products, or a sibling set of its own.

positions.says: Starting from /design-release-2.1/create-notification?category=germinal-products redirects to the shared flat origin page.
Germinal products is its own set at /germinal-products; the prototype's flat paths and ?category= routing are not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: germinal products is a sibling set at /germinal-products with the live-animals slugs, started from its own route. The prototype's behaviour (skipping the type question, landing on origin, back to the germinal list) is kept; only its URL and query shape are not copied, so the trace claim still backs req-127 and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether germinal-only behaviour depends on every chosen species being germinal, with mixed live-and-germinal consignments getting the live lists.

positions.says: The temperature question shows only when every selected species is germinal; a mixed consignment gets none.
A notification counts as germinal only when every selected species is germinal; a mix gets the full live-animal reason and purpose lists.
A saved reason becomes incomplete if the notification later turns germinal-only and the reason is not in the germinal list.
Each set holds one category, so a mixed consignment is never written, and every mixed-load criterion is dropped (req-124, req-169, req-170, req-181).

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the germinal set holds only germinal products, so its temperature question, two reasons and four purposes always apply, and there is no mixed case or later switch to germinal-only. The prototype's mixed-load conditions are set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether embryos and ova are one 'Embryos/Ova' catalogue item or two.

positions.says: Every germinal commodity is named '<Animal>, Embryos/Ova' or '<Animal>, Semen', 15 in all.
V4 lists 'Embryos/Ova - Cattle' as one entry under 5119985, among its twelve germinal entries.
Embryos and ova are separate items in the germinal catalogue; the prototype's single Embryos/Ova item is mock data and is not copied.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: embryos and ova are separate catalogue items, each with its own GBN-AG typeCode (EMBRYO, OVA), named '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova'. The prototype's 15-item Embryos/Ova naming is set aside. V4's entry still backs which animals have embryos and ova, so it is not overruled. The 9 October afternoon ruling applies the split only once the catalogue is re-distilled from MDM; until then today's combined lines stay and carry EMBRYO (c-282).

conflicts.about: Which germinal commodities the catalogue holds: V4's 12 'Applicable to' entries, or Design Release 2.1's 15, which add Cat and Dog embryos/ova.

positions.says: The twelve Applicable to entries are embryos/ova of Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep and semen of Cattle, Dog or Cat, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rodent/Rabbit and Sheep; whether this is the complete set the journey offers is not stated.
Cat, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Felis catus) is a germinal commodity.
Dog, Embryos/Ova (05119985, Canis familiaris) is a germinal commodity.
The prototype's single 'Embryos/Ova' items are mock data and are not copied.

conflicts.outcome: Once commodities come from MDM, the germinal products catalogue holds V4's 12 germinal commodities only, with embryos and ova split (ruling 9 October) and V4's 'Semen - Dog or Cat' shown as Design Release 2.1's separate Cat, Semen and Dog, Semen: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep embryos and ova, and Cat, Cattle, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep semen, 18 items. Cat and Dog embryos and ova are not offered: they come only from the prototype's Embryos/Ova mock data, which the 9 October ruling says is not copied, and V4, which outranks the prototype on what data the germinal set captures and where it applies, gives them no fields. Every V4 germinal field (temperature and the four Unit Level identifiers) therefore applies to every item in the catalogue, all five of V4's applicability lists naming the same twelve entries. The 18-item catalogue waits on MDM (c-282); meanwhile the germinal set offers today's 12 germinal lines.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal total gross weight is asked once for the notification (V4) or once per species line (Design Release 2.1).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) applies at Notification level, the only germinal row that does.
The germinal section uses three levels: notification level for the total gross weight, commodity level for the quantity and temperature, and unit level for the four identifiers.
Each germinal species asks Total gross weight in its own field.
Each germinal line has its own gross weight, stored but not published.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and speaks of each line's gross weight, which Design Release 2.1 also asks per species (the real store holds one line per species). The weight is asked and stored per species line; V4's notification-level placement is set aside. V4's three-level claim is not overruled: its commodity-level and unit-level placements still stand and back req-123, req-124 and req-251.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal Total gross weight and Temperature are required (Design Release 2.1) or optional (V4).

positions.says: Total gross weight (kg) is optional.
Temperature is optional.
Quantity (unit/pieces) is the only mandatory field in the germinal section.
Total gross weight is required: blank shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
Temperature is required: none chosen shows 'Select a temperature'.
A blank weight shows 'Enter the total gross weight'.
No temperature shows 'Select a temperature'.
The blank-field errors appear in order weight, packages, temperature.
Continuing with nothing entered shows 'Enter the total gross weight', 'Enter the number of packages', 'Select a temperature'.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype and is the policy for whether a germinal field is mandatory; mandatory status is validation, which the prototype does not decide. Total gross weight and Temperature are optional, with no blank errors, and neither holds back the Commodity details task's Complete status (req-1763) nor appears in the error summary's order (req-1762). Number of packages stays required (V4: mandatory to proceed, and the only mandatory field in its germinal section), so its blank error stands (req-1787). The prototype's germinal completeness bar on weight and temperature (prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-053, weighed in the commodity details area, whose live-animals half still stands) is set aside for the germinal set by the same reasoning.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal temperature is one answer per page (Design Release 2.1) or one per commodity line (V4).

positions.says: Temperature applies at Commodity Level, so each commodity line carries one.
Temperature is one radio group for the whole page, unlike weight and packages, which are per species.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the trace and decides data: every commodity line carries a temperature. Design Release 2.1 decides layout: the page asks the question once. Both are kept: the one answer is stored on every line. Neither claim is set aside.

conflicts.about: What a germinal line's quantity is: its number of packages, or its weight in kilograms.

positions.says: A germinal notification captures a 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' field, held on each commodity line.
Each germinal species asks 'Number of packages', the only count on the page.
The germinal 'decimal kilogram quantity' is stored but not published, because v0.2.0's quantity is a whole number.
The germinal weight is a total gross weight in kilograms held as a decimal.

conflicts.outcome: A germinal line's quantity is its number of packages: the page asks 'Number of packages', as Design Release 2.1 words it, and it takes V4's Quantity (unit/pieces) rules (required to proceed, a whole number from 1, at most 1,000). Being a whole number already carried by gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0, it fills that profile's quantity on GBN-AG. 'Total gross weight' is the line's gross weight in kilograms, stored as a decimal and shown in the service but not published, which is what ruling 2026-10-09 means by the decimal kilogram quantity: claim 22 makes weight, not quantity, the kilogram figure, and claim 42 only keeps it out of PIMS.

conflicts.about: When a germinal species counts as identified: once its entry is saved even if blank (Design Release 2.1), or once it holds at least one identifier (V4).

positions.says: A germinal notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for Complete and for submit.
A germinal species counts as identified once its entry is saved, even with every field empty.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling and V4 rank above the prototype: a germinal species counts as identified, for Complete and for submit, once its one entry holds at least one of the four identifiers. Each field stays optional on its own, so a blank entry still saves, but it does not count. The prototype's empty-entry rule is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether a germinal products notification with only one species selected may be submitted, and show its Identification details task Complete, with no identification details.

positions.says: A germinal products notification must be submitted with at least one germinal identifier per animal.
The section never says which of its fields count as a germinal identifier, nor how 'per animal' maps to the unit records the fields are captured at.
No row of the germinal table carries the submit-time rule: the quantity is the only mandatory field and the other six, the four identifiers included, are Optional.
One identifier is enough: a record with one identifier counts as identified, for the Complete status and for submit.

conflicts.outcome: V4 ranks above the prototype and is the policy for which germinal data is mandatory, and the 9 October ruling, ranking above V4, settles V4's own silence: V4 states the submit-time rule in its opening paragraph but carries it on no row and marks all four identifiers Optional, so the ruling sets the bar at one identifier and exempts no species. Every selected germinal species, a lone one included, needs its entry to hold at least one of the four identifiers before submit, and the Identification details task shows Complete on that same bar (req-261); the germinal review names any species short of it, however many are selected (req-1841). Under either reading of V4's 'per animal' (per species line or per notification) a single-species notification needs an identifier, so no question is left. The prototype's lone-species exemption (prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070, p11-056) is weighed in the identification and review areas, where it still sets the live-animals rule; it is not copied into the germinal set.

conflicts.about: Whether the INS germinal products list's 'Create new' starts the germinal set in this programme.

positions.says: The INS germinal list's 'Create new' starts the germinal set.
The INS germinal list's 'Create new' and the INS home's germinal section leave this programme with the INS home.
The germinal set's own copy of the reframed list sits at the set root, and its 'Create new' starts a germinal notification.
The type question's Germinal option stays the way into a germinal notification.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first and withdraws the earlier claim: a germinal notification is started from the type question's Germinal products option or from 'Create new' on the germinal set's own list at /germinal-products, and the origin page's back link returns to that list. The INS germinal list's 'Create new' is not built in this programme.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal set offers V4's 18-item catalogue, with embryos and ova separate, now, or today's 12 germinal lines until commodities come from MDM.

positions.says: The germinal data applies to twelve named germinal commodities, embryos/ova of five species and semen of seven species groups.
Embryos and ova are separate items in the germinal catalogue.
V4's 18-item germinal catalogue waits on MDM.
Embryos and ova as separate items applies only once the catalogue is re-distilled; until then combined lines carry EMBRYO.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: the germinal set goes ahead on today's 12 germinal lines (req-1927), whose combined 'Embryos/Ova' lines carry the interim typeCode EMBRYO and semen lines SEMEN (req-1928). V4's 18-item catalogue, its search and the separate EMBRYO and OVA lines (req-093, req-1782, req-1783, req-1800) are adopted but blocked until commodities come from MDM. Nothing is overruled: V4's list and the separate-items claim still back those blocked requirements.

conflicts.about: Whether the germinal collection and production dates get the MoJ date picker's 'Choose date' calendar now.

positions.says: The two germinal date fields use the MOJ date picker, with a 'Choose date' calendar toggle.
The germinal dates are built now as single text inputs; the 'Choose date' calendar waits on design question 12, because MoJ advises against its date picker for dates read from a document.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: each germinal date is built now as a single text input with the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026' and V4's checks (req-252, req-2097), and the calendar is its own increment in the waiting-on-design theme (req-253), built as design answers or dropped. The trace is not overruled: it still describes what design is asked to keep.

conflicts.about: Whether the same-checks rule for Save and return to overview reaches the germinal products set, which the 26 October ruling does not name.

positions.says: The same-checks rule applies on every page that has both buttons, in the live animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend.
The ruling says nothing about the germinal-products set or any other frontend with both save buttons, so whether the rule reaches them is left open.
Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals feature folder, taken after the live twin is built, plus the germinal differences.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. The 26 October ruling's 'no page is an exception' and the 9 October ruling's copy rule both point at the germinal set, and the copied live-animals pages carry the behaviour with them, but the set's germinal-only pages (Commodity details and Identification details) are written in this programme rather than copied, so their save behaviour is not settled by the copy alone, and the ruling's own stated scope omits the set.
conflicts.question: Does Save and return to overview make exactly the same checks as Save and continue in the germinal products set, including on its own Commodity details and Identification details pages?
conflicts.default: Every page in the germinal products set that shows both buttons makes the same checks on each: the copied live-animals pages carry the behaviour from the copy, and the set's own Commodity details and Identification details pages are built with it, so the germinal weight, package, length and date rules are made on both buttons alike.

conflicts.about: Whether a germinal commodity's code is the seven-digit number V4 writes or the eight-digit code the real catalogue and MDM carry.

positions.says: The twelve germinal entries are written as 5111000 and 5119985, with their leading zero dropped, and the page never says how they map to the codes a notification carries.
Cattle semen is 05111000, the only germinal commodity not under 05119985.
V4's 18-item germinal catalogue waits on MDM.
The rest of the commodities area goes ahead on today's commodity data.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first: a germinal commodity's code is whatever the catalogue carries, today's commodity data now and MDM's once commodities come from it, which is the eight-digit 05111000 for cattle semen and 05119985 for every other germinal commodity, shown with its leading zero as Design Release 2.1 shows it. V4's seven-digit 5111000 and 5119985 are the same codes with the leading zero dropped, and no code is edited in the service to match the page. Nothing is overruled: V4's entries still back which germinal commodities the data applies to, and its gap claim still records that the page states no mapping, which is why the catalogue rather than the page decides the code.
